title: CHANGELOG.md has no Unreleased section, so four post-tag changes are recorded nowhere
description:
The instance repair for the gap QCLI-286 tracks the mechanism of. Filed separately because QCLI-286 acceptance criteria are all about a CHECK -- a pre-tag mechanism, its runbook placement, and its CI wiring -- and repairing todays CHANGELOG is not one of them. Work outside a tasks acceptance criteria is a new task, not a silent addition.

FOUND WHILE VERIFYING SOMETHING ELSE, which is the only reason anyone looked. opum-fleet reported on 2026-09-15 that it cannot detect QCLI-316 new top-level "scope" key from the installed quest, because dev package.json declares 0.7.1 and so does the published build that lacks it (QCLI-296). Checking whether any OTHER surface could have told them, I found the second one blank too.

MEASURED. The v0.7.1 tag peels to 9258018, which is the release-prep commit itself. Three commits since it touch src/, and one more rewrites a file that ships inside the published package. None is mentioned anywhere in CHANGELOG.md:

  e9c3c62  feat(QCLI-316)  task list gains a top-level "scope" key on every listing envelope
  8f474ef  fix(QCLI-313)   checklist replacement refuses an edit that would silently clear a box
  5544ac3  fix(QCLI-315)   agent-guide prose contradicted the flag it documents
  0c3117f  fix(QCLI-307)   README.md no longer ships a stale version; gated at pack time

CAUSE, and it is ADJACENT TO QCLI-286, not identical. QCLI-286 diagnoses a ROLLED-FORWARD version section: 0.6.1 content reused under 0.6.2, so later work had no empty heading to land under. Here the 0.7.1 section is correct and correctly finalized. The defect is that release prep RENAMED "## Unreleased" into "## 0.7.1" and left no successor behind, so there is currently no Unreleased section at all. Different cause, identical consequence -- and it argues for a fix cheaper than either option QCLI-286 AC1 names: release prep must leave a fresh empty "## Unreleased" heading behind when it renames one. That step is absent from docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, and its absence is what produced this occurrence.

WHY IT IS NOT TIDINESS. A consumer had two surfaces that could have told it "scope" exists and is unreleased -- the version string and the changelog -- and both were silent, for two unrelated reasons. It wrote a key-presence workaround instead. That workaround is correct and should stay (the envelope is an open key set), but it was written blind.

acceptanceCriteria.text: CHANGELOG.md on dev carries an Unreleased section naming every change since the v0.7.1 tag that a consumer can observe, verified by listing commits in 9258018..dev that touch src/ or a packaged file and confirming each appears
The Unreleased section states for QCLI-316 that scope is additive and detectable by key presence, so a reader learns how to consume it and not merely that it exists
docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md instructs release prep to leave a fresh empty Unreleased heading behind when it renames one into a version heading, at the step where the rename happens
The runbook change is written as a step in the procedure rather than as a warning, so following the procedure produces the heading without anyone remembering to

plan: 1. Restore the ## Unreleased heading in CHANGELOG.md above ## 0.7.1, with Added/Fixed subsections matching the files existing shape.

2. Write one entry per consumer-observable change in 9258018..dev: QCLI-316 (scope, Added), QCLI-313, QCLI-315, QCLI-307 (Fixed). Derive the list from git log against src/ and packaged files rather than from memory, and state for QCLI-316 that scope is detectable by key presence because that is how the one known consumer already reads it.

3. Add the missing step to docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md: Step 5 renames ## Unreleased to ## <version> AND leaves a fresh empty ## Unreleased behind it. Step 5 currently gives no changelog instruction at all -- only the What a version bump touches note at line 190 mentions the rename, and it does not mention the successor.
4. Run bun run check and lore check; commit tracker writes alongside.
5. Open the PR, wait newest-per-context on the head SHA, close QCLI-319 in that same PR citing the PR number and run id.

finalSummary:
CHANGELOG.md on dev now carries an Unreleased section covering all four consumer-observable changes that landed after the v0.7.1 tag, and the release runbook now produces the successor heading as a step rather than relying on anyone remembering it.

WHAT CHANGED.

1. CHANGELOG.md gains `## Unreleased` above `## 0.7.1`, with Added (QCLI-316 scope) and Fixed (QCLI-313, QCLI-315, QCLI-307) subsections. Its preamble states plainly that nothing below it is published and that 0.7.1 predates every entry, so a consumer running the published CLI observes none of them -- the fact that was unavailable from any surface when opum-fleet went looking.

2. docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md step 5 is rewritten from "Require the native-execution receipt..." to "Finalize the changelog, then tag", opening with the rename-plus-successor edit and showing the two-line result. The "What a version bump touches" note at line 190 now says the tag-time move is a RENAME PLUS A NEW HEADING rather than a rename.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED, and one correction worth keeping.

Criterion 1 was checked by script, not by reading: git log 9258018..origin/dev over src/, README.md, package.json, bin/, npm/ yields exactly {QCLI-307, QCLI-313, QCLI-315, QCLI-316}, and each id was then searched for inside the extracted Unreleased section.

The FIRST run of that script reported all four MISSING. The defect was in the script, not the file: it delimited the section with ch.index("## 0.7.1"), which matched the backticked "## 0.7.1" inside the new prose explaining what release prep renamed. Re-run with a line-anchored `^## ` heading match, all four are PRESENT and the section is 6016 chars rather than the 302 the broken delimiter produced. Recording it because the failure direction was the safe one only by luck -- a section-extractor that silently returns a 302-char prefix would, on a different edit, have reported PRESENT for a section it never read.

Criteria 2-4 verified by reading the produced text: the QCLI-316 entry states scope is additive and tells the reader to detect it by key presence rather than by version, naming why a version gate cannot work (dev declares 0.7.1 and so does the published build that lacks the key, QCLI-296). The runbook change sits at the rename step and is written imperatively ("add a fresh empty ## Unreleased heading directly above it in the same edit"), with the rationale following the instruction rather than standing in for it.

Gates: bun run check exits 0, 535 pass / 0 fail. lore check exits 0, 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

SCOPE NOTE. This is the instance repair only. QCLI-286 still owns the mechanism -- a pre-tag CHECK that catches the class -- and remains To Do; this change makes the omission harder to commit but adds no gate that would catch it.
